cm-3-001.gate_key: past_simple | B1.1 | text | Correct the mistake. Keep *yesterday*: I have seen this film yesterday, so let's watch something else tonight. |

accepted: I saw this film yesterday, so let's watch something else tonight.
I watched this film yesterday, so let's watch something else tonight.

item.q: Correct the mistake. Keep *yesterday*: I have seen this film yesterday, so let's watch something else tonight.
item.why: *yesterday* is a finished time: past simple (*I saw*, *I watched*), not *I have seen*.
item.why_lv: *yesterday* ir pabeigts laiks: Past Simple (*I saw, I watched*), nevis *I have seen.*
answers: I saw this film yesterday, so let's watch something else tonight.
I watched this film yesterday, so let's watch something else tonight.

cm-3-003.gate_key: future | A2.2 | text | Correct the mistake: It's late. I walk you to the bus stop. |

accepted: It's late. I'll walk you to the bus stop.
It's late. I will walk you to the bus stop.
It's late. I can walk you to the bus stop.
It's late. Let me walk you to the bus stop.

item.q: Correct the mistake: It's late. I walk you to the bus stop.
item.why: An offer you decide on now: *will*, *I'll walk you*. *I can walk you …* is an offer too.
item.why_lv: Piedāvājums, ko izlem tagad: *will, I'll walk you*. *I can walk you* … arī ir piedāvājums.
answer_notes: It's late. Let me walk you to the bus stop.
Also correct: *Let me walk you* is an offer too. With *I*, the offer needs *will*: *I'll walk you*.
Arī pareizi: *Let me walk you* arī ir piedāvājums. Ar *I* piedāvājumam vajag *will*: *I'll walk you*.
answers: It's late. I'll walk you to the bus stop.
It's late. I will walk you to the bus stop.
It's late. I can walk you to the bus stop.
It's late. Let me walk you to the bus stop.

cm-3-004.gate_key: future | B1.1 | text | Correct the mistake: I can't go out until the plumber will come, so could you buy some bread? |

accepted: I can't go out until the plumber comes, so could you buy some bread?
I can't go out until the plumber has come, so could you buy some bread?

item.q: Correct the mistake: I can't go out until the plumber will come, so could you buy some bread?
item.why: After *until* we use the present, also about the future: *until the plumber comes*, not *will come*.
item.why_lv: Aiz *until* lieto tagadni, arī runājot par nākotni: *until the plumber comes*, nevis *will come*. Latviski kamēr atnāks ir nākotnē, tāpēc gribas *will*.
answer_notes: I can't go out until the plumber has come, so could you buy some bread?
Also correct: *has come* says the plumber's visit will be over.
Arī pareizi: *has come* saka, ka santehniķis jau būs atnācis.
answers: I can't go out until the plumber comes, so could you buy some bread?
I can't go out until the plumber has come, so could you buy some bread?
